keyVerseText: And blessed be the most high God, which hath delivered thine enemies into thy hand. And he gave him tithes of all.
rootMeaning: The root of מָגַן (mâgan) is derived denominatively from מָגֵן (mâgên), which literally means shield or buckler. This root conveys the idea of protection and defense, often represented by a physical shield. Beyond the common English gloss of 'deliver,' the root sense implies an encompassing or shielding action, suggesting not merely rescue but a protective handing over or safeguarding from harm.
usageInScripture: The verb מָגַן appears three times in the Hebrew Scriptures, consistently conveying the act of delivering or handing over, often in the context of rescue or surrender. Its translations such as 'which hath delivered,' 'shall she deliver,' and 'how shall I deliver' reveal a range that includes both divine deliverance and human action. This consistency highlights the term's emphasis on the act of transferring someone or something into safety or into the hands of another, often adversarial, party.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding מָגַן as rooted in the imagery of a shield enriches our comprehension of divine deliverance as not only rescue but also protection. God is portrayed as the ultimate shield who delivers His people by encompassing them with His power and care. This verb underscores the relational dynamic of surrendering to God's protective hand, emphasizing trust in His sovereign defense. For believers, it reflects the assurance that deliverance is both an act of salvation and a shielded refuge, pointing ultimately to Christ as our defender and deliverer.
keyVerseReflection: Genesis 14:20 declares, 'And blessed be the most high God, which hath delivered thine enemies into thy hand.' Here, מָגַן highlights God's sovereign act of handing over adversaries, portraying Him as the divine shield who not only rescues but also empowers His people by delivering foes into their control. This word enriches the verse by emphasizing God's protective and delivering power, affirming His role as the ultimate source of victory and security.
